passage:
Tuesday. Manoj called Dhruv an hour before the cricket match. "So you'd rather play than help me with my project? Fine. I'll do it alone, like always. Nobody cares." Dhruv felt his stomach drop and stayed home.
The next Monday. Same pattern: Manoj sighed loudly in the canteen about being abandoned until Dhruv gave up his lunch hour to sit with him. Afterwards Dhruv realised he could not remember the last time he had said no and been forgiven quickly.
Friday. "I can help on Saturday morning for two hours," Dhruv said. "I can't drop everything every time." Manoj went silent, then said, "Real friends would do more." Dhruv's hands were shaky, but he said, "I'm still here for those two hours." On Sunday a meme arrived from Manoj.

qa.q: How long did Dhruv offer to help on Saturday morning?
qa.a: He offered to help for two hours.

qa.q: Why did Dhruv's stomach drop when Manoj called before the match?
qa.a: He felt guilty and afraid of letting a friend down, because Manoj framed the choice as Dhruv not caring. That is why he gave up the match.

qa.q: What could Dhruv try if Manoj keeps using guilt?
qa.a: He can keep naming what he will and will not do, like the two hours, and repeat it calmly. Friends who respect him will accept a no.

qa.q: How might Manoj see Dhruv's new limit?
qa.a: Manoj may feel hurt or worried about losing the support he is used to, which could explain the line about real friends. The meme on Sunday suggests he did not want to end things.

grounding: A friend uses guilt and drama to keep the protagonist close, and he starts naming what he will and will not do.

passage: At 10:40 p.m. Afreen's phone lit up again: 'Guess I'll just sit alone on my birthday eve. Classic.' Chaitanya had sent six messages since Afreen said no to riding across Hyderabad for a late-night cake run; Afreen's exam was at nine the next morning. This was how it usually went. Skip a lecture to sit with Chaitanya after a fight at home. Lend the scooter again. Cancel on other friends because Chaitanya 'was having a terrible week'. Each yes bought a few calm days. Tonight Afreen sat on the bed in the rented room in Tolichowki, typing and deleting. Finally: 'Happy early birthday. I'm not coming tonight because of my exam. I'll take you for breakfast on Saturday.' The reply came fast: 'wow ok'. Afreen put the phone in a drawer and opened the revision notes.

qa.q: At what time was Afreen's exam the next morning?
qa.a: Afreen's exam was at nine the next morning.

qa.q: What might Afreen be feeling while typing and deleting?
qa.a: Afreen feels guilty and torn, used to buying calm days by saying yes, yet sure the exam matters.

qa.q: What made Afreen's final message a good boundary?
qa.a: It said clearly what Afreen would not do and offered something Afreen would do, breakfast on Saturday, without apologising for the exam.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya see Afreen's no?
qa.a: Chaitanya seems to take it as being abandoned on a birthday eve, and the 'wow ok' shows hurt used as pressure rather than respect for the no.

grounding: Shows a friend using guilt and drama to keep Afreen close, and Afreen stating what will and will not happen instead of appeasing again.

passage:
'You picked them over me,' Joseph said, blocking the library stairs. 'After everything I did for you in first year.'
'I picked a project group, Joseph. Yours was full.'
'You could've asked me to make space. You didn't even think of me.'
'I did think of you. I asked on Monday, and you said you'd see.'
'Fine. I'll do everything alone. Like always.'
Uma felt the old pull to say sorry, to switch groups, to fix it. It had worked before; it always cost something.
'Joseph, I care about you. I'm staying in my group. And I'm happy to study with you on Thursday, like always.'
'So that's it?'
'That's what I can do. If you're upset, I'll listen. But I'm not switching.'
Joseph looked away, then muttered, 'Thursday, then.'

qa.q: When did Uma ask Joseph about joining Joseph's group?
What does 'the old pull to say sorry' suggest about how Uma feels?
qa.a: It suggests Uma feels guilty and anxious under Joseph's reproach, tempted to smooth things over the way it worked before.

qa.q: What would you advise Uma if Joseph brings up first year again?
qa.a: Thank Joseph for the past kindness but keep the no, the way Uma offered Thursday study instead of switching groups.

qa.q: What is it like for Joseph when Uma holds firm?
qa.a: Joseph feels left out and hurt, and seems surprised that guilt did not work, grudgingly accepting Thursday.

grounding: Shows a friend using guilt about past favours to pull Uma back, and Uma naming what Uma will and will not do while staying kind.
